Animal travel needs calm handling and clear steps.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: This section sets the handling rules for animal check-in, flight handoff, and reporting.

Use a warm, steady tone with travelers and keep the animal secure while the passenger completes the counter steps. For boarding, use FM-597 at the desk before you clear the animal for the next step. Check the carrier, the tag, and the reservation match before you release the traveler from the counter. If a traveler arrives with missing papers, stop the process and direct them to fix the issue before the handoff continues. Keep the cabin team informed when an animal is accepted, and note any special handling in the shift log in plain language.

For incident reporting, the Claim Adjudicator handles the report and records the next step. If there is a delay, a carrier fault, a distress event, or a complaint, write a clear account right away and include the names of the traveler and pet when those names are provided. Keep the facts short, exact, and free of guesswork. Do not promise a result or a timeline. Send the report through the normal desk channel and tell the next shift what is pending before you leave the station.

When travelers ask for help, answer in direct words and keep the line moving. If Samuel Svensson, Nora Khan, or Coco are involved, treat the file with the same rules and the same calm attention as any other case. Seal all forms after use, return unused supplies to the drawer, and leave the counter ready for the next handoff. Contact the shift lead or the duty supervisor if a case needs review.
